name: Atlassian: pull organization audit log
description: Every 5 minutes, reads new Atlassian organization audit-log events (sign-ins, admin, user and policy changes across Jira, Confluence and the org) and creates one info alert per event. Add suppression rules for the actions you don't need.

params.label: Organization ID
params.help: Shown when you create the API key (also in the admin.atlassian.com URL).

secrets.name: ATLASSIAN_ADMIN_API_KEY
secrets.description: Atlassian organization admin API key (sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`). Atlassian Administration > Settings > API keys.

setup:
### Atlassian side
1. admin.atlassian.com > your organization > **Settings > API keys > Create API key**. A key **with scopes** needs the audit-log read scope; a key without scopes can call every admin API, so prefer scopes. Keys last at most one year.
2. Copy the **API key** and the **Organization ID** (shown once).

### Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add `ATLASSIAN_ADMIN_API_KEY` (allowed host `api.atlassian.com`).
2. Install with `ATLASSIAN_ORG_ID`.

### What it does
`GET https://api.atlassian.com/admin/v1/orgs/<org>/events-stream?from=<previous run, epoch ms>&limit=200&sortOrder=asc` (the polling endpoint; Atlassian rate-limits audit-log calls per minute). Each event becomes an alert with source `atlassian`, external id = the event `id`, title = `<action> by <actor email or name>` and severity **info**: Atlassian events carry no severity, so triage them with suppression rules (e.g. `payload.attributes.action equals <noisy action>`). Only the first 200 new events per run are read; a busy org may need a shorter interval.

Docs relied on:
- Admin API keys: https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/manage-an-organization-with-the-admin-apis/
- Organization REST API (OpenAPI): https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/admin/organization/rest/intro/
